title: LIVE SURFACE CURRENTS
noaa_source: NOAA/NOS Great Lakes Operational Forecast System (GLOFS: LSOFS/LMHOFS/LEOFS/LOOFS) surface-current nowcast + NOAA/GLERL experimental GLCFS-FVCOM Huron-Erie Corridor & lower St. Marys River nowcast fill
product_name: NOAA/NOS Great Lakes Operational Forecast System (GLOFS: LSOFS/LMHOFS/LEOFS/LOOFS) surface-current nowcast + NOAA/GLERL experimental GLCFS-FVCOM Huron-Erie Corridor & lower St. Marys River nowcast fill
variable: u_eastward / v_northward surface-layer velocity components (filed m/s, direction of water motion TOWARD); speed = sqrt(U^2+V^2), displayed in cm/s; dense 1 px streamlets trace RK2 streamlines through the filed (U,V) field, micro-chevrons mark downstream direction
units: cm/s display (source m/s x100); direction deg TOWARD
spatial_resolution_source: operational GLOFS regular grids ~0.5-1.1 km; experimental FVCOM 30 m-2 km unstructured
spatial_resolution_rendered: 1800x1175 canvas over lon [-93.0,-73.5], lat [40.5,49.5] (mean-value binning, no upsampling of source precision)
missing_data_treatment: fill value -99999, land mask, and out-of-domain cells rendered fully transparent; experimental fill only where operational has no vector; never zero-filled.
shoreline_mask: assets/great_lakes_watermask.png — shared NOAA medium-resolution shoreline water mask (nautical-chart compilation, mean-high-water datum; snapped + polygonized once, full vertex precision, antialiased). Overlay alpha is multiplied by this mask and edge RGB is bled into transparent pixels (anti-fringe for bilinear clients), so every product shares one shoreline.
attribution: Data: US NOAA. This project is not endorsed by NOAA. See DATA_SOURCES.md for exact products and endpoints.
legend_scale_html: Surface-current speed (centimeters per second, one continuous gradient): LOWEST 0 dark-blue stagnant → 10 teal → 20 yellow → 30 orange → 50 red → 75 red-violet → HIGHEST+ 100 cm/s dark-purple channel jets. Same speed always shows the same color; above 100 stays dark-purple. Thousands of fine white streaks RIDE the flow — each traces a short RK2 streamline of the filed U/V field (brighter streak = faster water), with tiny chevrons pointing downstream. Now: max 219, median 13.0 cm/s, median flow 164° (S). NO DATA stays transparent — never zero.
direction_convention: u_eastward = CF eastward_sea_water_velocity, v_northward = CF northward_sea_water_velocity (m/s, direction water moves TOWARD); FVCOM u/v are the same eastward/northward motion components. Arrows follow (U,V) directly with no FROM->TOWARD reversal; toward-heading = atan2(U,V) clockwise from north.
arrow_method: No preset lattice. Deterministic jittered seeds (seeded RNG) advected downstream along RK2-midpoint streamlines (3 px steps, up to 40 steps ≈ 120 px paths) integrated through the filed U/V field with bilinear sampling; each accepted path is drawn as a 1 px streamlet, every third path carries a tiny downstream chevron. Traces stop at land/no-data, stagnant water (<1 cm/s), or hairpins. Streamlet brightness encodes speed (dim drift, bright jets); rivers get denser seeds. Glyphs trace the same field as the gradient colors.
river_treatment: The shared open-lake shoreline mask reads land over sub-pixel rivers, so river alpha is restored product-locally ONLY where an authoritative source vector exists inside the documented RIVER_BOXES (St. Marys, St. Clair, Detroit, Niagara). Shared mask asset untouched; no other layer affected.
field_type: model-generated nowcast guidance (FVCOM-based GLOFS/GLCFS), NOT direct observations

lsofs.role: Lake Superior + upper St. Marys River

leofs.role: Lake Erie + upper Niagara River mouth

hec.role: St. Clair River + Lake St. Clair + Detroit River

coverage_gaps: St. Marys rapids/locks reach (~46.35-46.42): no model vectors
Niagara Falls/gorge reach (~42.905-43.23): no model vectors
Welland Canal / Trent-Severn / other minor canals: no coverage
folder_html:
LIVE SURFACE CURRENTS

How fast the surface water is moving right now (color = speed, brighter streaks = faster) and which way it flows (thousands of fine flow streaks with tiny downstream chevrons). Covers all five Great Lakes plus the connecting rivers and channels where NOAA models provide current vectors.

Surface-current speed (centimeters per second, one continuous gradient): LOWEST 0 dark-blue stagnant → 10 teal → 20 yellow → 30 orange → 50 red → 75 red-violet → HIGHEST+ 100 cm/s dark-purple channel jets. Same speed always shows the same color; above 100 stays dark-purple. Thousands of fine white streaks RIDE the flow — each traces a short RK2 streamline of the filed U/V field (brighter streak = faster water), with tiny chevrons pointing downstream. Now: max 219, median 13.0 cm/s, median flow 164° (S). NO DATA stays transparent — never zero.

Units: cm/s (speed gradient + streamlet brightness; chevrons show downstream direction)
